summary: Butte County tower built 1925 by the state, county and Forest Service; still listed standing; NHLR-registered 2019; current access not confirmed.

facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A July 1924 report says 14 miles northeast of Oroville; March 1925 reports say 20 miles from Oroville. Both are reported in the story and neither is treated as settled.
The July 1924 plan said a 70-foot station; March 1925 reports and the June 1925 completion report describe a 60-foot tower (60 feet above the summit). The record's 18.3 m (60 ft) is kept.
A June 1925 paper gives the summit as 3040 feet (the same paper gives the base as 2980 feet); the NHLR gives 3,005 ft (916 m). The record's 915.9 m matches the NHLR and is kept.

notes_for_editor: History is well sourced (NHLR plus 1924-1939 newspaper transcriptions, which are secondary and were not checked against the original papers). Current access and rental status were not found in the sources read, so there is no access or visit block. Camera feeds named Bloomer Lookout appear online (ALERTCalifornia, opencctv) but I could not confirm they sit on this tower, so they are left out. Staffing names come from the transcriptions only. The dedication date was corrected from early July to June 1925: the June 24, 1925 Gridley Herald reports a Saturday dedication with Pratt giving the speech, and the July 5 article describes the same event later.
